title: Bigger Benefits or Bigger Paychecks? What Employees Really Value.
summary: Do employees prefer higher salaries or better benefits? Learn how benefits influence employee satisfaction, retention, financial wellness, and overall compensation value.
body_markdown:
Listen to the Article: Bigger Benefits or Bigger Paychecks? What Employees Really Value.


6:18


Small business owners face a difficult balancing act. Employees want competitive pay, but they also want benefits that help protect their health and financial well-being. When budgets are limited, employers may feel forced to choose between bigger paychecks and better benefits.


The reality is that employees want both. They evaluate the overall value of their compensation package, including what they earn today and the protection available when unexpected expenses arise.


## Financial Stress Extends Beyond the Paycheck


### Why aren't higher wages always enough to reduce employee financial stress?


Employees are managing rising costs in nearly every part of their lives, and healthcare is a significant concern. According to


[MetLife’s 2025 U.S. Employee Benefit Trends Study](https://www.metlife.com/about-us/newsroom/2025/march/economic-concerns-lower-us-workforce-health-and-productivity-raising-need-for-employee-employer-trust-new-metlife-study/) , 77% of employees identified rising medical costs as a source of stress, while 68% cited economic uncertainty. The study also found that employees are looking to their employers for stability and support.


Higher wages can help employees manage immediate expenses, but wages alone may not protect them from the financial impact of an illness, injury, disability, or other unexpected event. Benefits can provide an additional layer of financial protection and help employees prepare for expenses that may otherwise be difficult to absorb.


## **Employer-Sponsored Benefits Have Significant Value**


### Why should employers view benefits as part of total compensation?


The value of a paycheck is easy to see. The value of employer-sponsored benefits can be less obvious, even though the employer’s investment may be substantial.


[KFF’s 2025 Employer Health Benefits Survey](https://www.kff.org/health-costs/2025-employer-health-benefits-survey/) found that the average annual premium for employer-sponsored family health coverage reached $26,993. Employees contributed an average of $6,850 toward that cost. The average annual premium for single coverage was $9,325.


These figures illustrate why health coverage is an important part of total compensation. An employee’s salary may be the most visible element of the package, but it does not reflect the full value an employer provides.


## **Different Employees Need Different Benefits**


### What benefits do different employees value most?


[What employees value most](https://www.bbsi.com/business-owner-resources/employee-benefit-statistics) often depends on their personal circumstances. A younger employee raising a family may appreciate accident insurance or hospital indemnity coverage, while an older employee may be more interested in critical illness protection or disability coverage. Some employees place a high value on comprehensive medical coverage, while others are looking for benefits that help protect their income or reduce financial stress during life's unexpected events.


Offering a diverse benefits package allows employees to select the coverage that is most meaningful to them, creating a more personalized and valuable total rewards experience.


## **Bridging the Gap for Business Owners**


### How can small businesses compete for talent without constantly increasing pay?


Most employees evaluate a job opportunity based on total compensation, which includes wages, health insurance, retirement benefits, disability protection, paid time off, and other employer-sponsored programs. While competitive pay remains important, benefits often influence how employees compare employers, especially when healthcare costs and economic uncertainty are top-of-mind concerns.


Benefits can also play an important role in employee retention. An employee may receive a modest pay increase elsewhere, but still choose to stay if their current employer offers strong health coverage, disability protection, voluntary benefits, and other programs that support their family and financial well-being.


For small businesses


[competing against larger employers](https://www.bbsi.com/business-owner-resources/how-to-develop-competitive-employee-benefits-program) for talent, benefits can help level the playing field. A thoughtfully designed benefits package may allow employers to attract and retain qualified employees without relying solely on wage increases.


When employees understand the value of their benefits and know how to use them, they are often better positioned to manage healthcare expenses and unexpected financial challenges. That can contribute to a stronger employee experience while helping employers build a more competitive total rewards strategy.

## Quick Summary


Employees don't want to choose between better benefits and bigger paychecks. They want a compensation package that supports both their immediate financial needs and their long-term well-being. While wages help cover everyday expenses, benefits provide valuable protection against healthcare costs, income disruptions, and unexpected life events. By offering competitive compensation alongside access to meaningful benefits, employers can create a stronger employee value proposition that supports recruitment, retention, and workforce satisfaction.


---


## Frequently Asked Questions About Employee Benefits


##### Do employees prefer better benefits or higher pay?


Most employees value both. While competitive wages help address day-to-day expenses, benefits provide financial protection and support that employees may not be able to afford on their own. Many workers evaluate the entire compensation package rather than salary alone.


##### Why are employee benefits important to workers?


Benefits can help employees manage healthcare costs, protect their income during unforeseen events, and reduce financial stress. Health insurance, disability coverage, and supplemental benefits often provide valuable financial support when employees need it most.


##### What benefits do employees value most?


The answer varies by individual. Commonly valued benefits include health insurance, disability coverage, life insurance, health savings accounts, flexible spending accounts, and voluntary benefits such as accident and critical illness insurance.


##### Can strong benefits help attract and retain employees?


Yes. Benefits are often a key factor when employees compare job opportunities. A comprehensive benefits package can help employers differentiate themselves in a competitive labor market and improve employee retention.


##### How can small businesses offer competitive benefits?


Partnering with organizations that provide access to larger-group benefits programs can help small businesses offer a wider range of coverage options. This may give employees access to benefits that are typically associated with larger employers.
